title: Explicit Profinite Presentation of the Absolute Galois Group of ℚ₂
aiSystem: Claude Fable 5 + OpenAI GPT-5.5 Pro + Lean 4
whyItMatters: Closes the missing dyadic p = 2 case left open for 44 years since Jannsen–Wingberg (1982), giving an explicit 4-generator, 2-relation presentation of G_{ℚ₂} verified by two independent Lean 4 formalizations.
summary: Posed by MIT mathematician David Roe on Epoch AI’s FrontierMath: Open Problems, finding an explicit profinite presentation of the absolute Galois group of the 2-adic numbers ℚ₂ had remained open for 44 years after Jannsen and Wingberg solved all odd primes p in 1982. After Claude Fable 5 produced the first verifier-passing candidate on June 9, 2026, David Turturean ran a 26-hour voice-directed ChatGPT Pro (GPT-5.5 Pro) session in mid-June that produced an explicit marked presentation (four generators σ, τ, x₀, x₁, the tame relation τ^σ = τ², one explicit wild relation, and a pro-2 wild condition) plus a 60-page proof. Roe and Turturean then independently verified the theorem via two separate Lean 4 formalizations and a 5,402-group finite-quotient verifier.
technicalHighlights: Gives an explicit marked profinite presentation of G_{ℚ₂} using four generators, two explicit word relations, and a pro-2 condition on wild generators—completing the local absolute Galois group program started in 1982.
Proof matches surjection counts onto every finite group via Fox–Jacobian calculus, local Tate duality, quadratic Gauss-sum comparisons, and Fourier inversion.
Verified at three independent levels: two separately initiated Lean 4 formalizations (down to 7–9 classical literature interfaces) plus exact finite-quotient checks across all 5,402 test groups.
caveats: The July 26, 2026 manuscript has not yet completed external journal peer review, and the two Lean 4 formalizations axiomatize 7–9 standard classical interfaces from local class field theory and Galois cohomology.

scoreRationale.ripple: Turns questions about 2-adic field extensions, counts, and local Langlands parameters into explicit finite group computations.
scoreRationale.verification: Independently checked by two separate Lean 4 formalizations plus exact extension counts on all 5,402 finite test groups.
scoreRationale.velocity: Solved in a 26-hour AI-assisted session after resisting explicit presentation since 1982.
